name: spike-s-goal-retrieval-cue-lexicon
status: FROZEN for design review. Any edit requires a version bump and a dated DECISIONS.md entry. Not yet ratified for implementation.
notes: Cue lexicon for goal-aware retrieval direction selection (Spike-S extension, D-0022).
Goal text may ONLY select a retrieval direction/class from a fixed enum. It never names symbols, files, or influences resolution.

Anti-gaming rule: no pattern may contain, match, or special-case any identifier, file name, or symbol name from fixture-1, fixture-2, or any gold set. Patterns are generic English retrieval-intent vocabulary only. Verified by scripts/check-cue-lexicon.js before any benchmark run.
Exactly one directional class fires per goal (priority order below). AMBIGUITY_EXPANSION and DEPTH are additive and always available.
Deterministic: all matches are case-insensitive; tie-breaks are span-then-pattern-id; no randomness, no scores.

defaults.defaultJustification: Incoming usage is the dominant retrieval intent; a bare seed name with no cue (e.g. a single identifier) means 'this and its usages'.

additiveBehaviors.AMBIGUITY_EXPANSION: If the seed symbol name maps to N same-name index symbols (overloads / cross-file duplicates), all N are included and references to that name contribute enclosing symbols with confidence=ambiguous. Always on (resolution-level behavior, not a cue).
additiveBehaviors.DEPTH: M1 raises dependees/chain walk depth from 1 to defaults.maxDepth (budget-bounded).

targetReferringTokens.seedName: case-insensitive word-boundary match of the seed symbol's name in the goal text

tieBreak.withinClass: earliest match span start; then longer match; then pattern id lexicographic
tieBreak.acrossClasses: priority list; the highest-priority class with at least one match wins and is the only direction applied

budgetBehavior.ranking: seed first; then hop distance ascending; then bindingKind rank (index-symbol > local-shadow > routed > unresolved); then symbolKey lexicographic
budgetBehavior.onTruncation: emit truncated=true with droppedCount; overall result confidence capped at heuristic

patterns.behavior: Scan: seed + enclosing index symbols of every binding-hard reference (bindingKind in {local-shadow, re-export-routed, default-routed, namespace-routed, unresolved-use}). Unresolved import declarations with no use site contribute no enclosing symbol but are reported in the audit.
patterns.note: Generic binding-failure intent. Category elaborations (shadowed/re-exported/default-imported) are deliberately NOT lexicon words.

patterns.behavior: Bidirectional one-hop walk: seed + enclosing symbols of references to the seed (referrers) + symbols the seed references (dependees). Depth 1 unless M1 also fires.
Seed only; if the seed is reached through a re-export route, return the origin symbol of the route.
Outgoing: seed + symbols the seed references (one hop; M1 extends depth).
Incoming: seed + enclosing index symbols of references to the seed. Same as the default direction.
Passive voice => the seed is the object being used: referrers. Position-independent.
Possessive incoming-actor noun: referrers. Disjoint from D2 by noun list (actors vs sources/inputs/dependencies).

Active verb; direction by position of the nearest target-referring token (seed name word-boundary or pronoun it/its/them/they): token AFTER the verb => REFERRERS ('everything that uses X'); token BEFORE the verb and none after => DEPENDEES ('X calls Y', 'which fmt overload does o call'); no target-referring token found => REFERRERS (fallback; incoming-usage is the dominant intent for bare active verbs, e.g. 'depend on the addition helper'). The resolved class then competes in the priority list. Past-participle forms (used/called/...) are excluded here; they belong to R2.
patterns.note: Past participles are matched only by R2 via the passive-auxiliary requirement, so 'called' never fires AV.

patterns.behavior: Additive: raises dependees/chain depth from 1 to defaults.maxDepth (6), budget-bounded.
